title: Perpetual yield exposure targets are declared to override the rest of the Stability Scope
content:
A.3.4.5.1 gives the Core Facilitator broad latitude to implement "various perpetual yield strategies, including on-chain and off-chain mechanisms, that enable the Sky Protocol to take advantage of high risk-adjusted return on perpetual yield strategies in the crypto markets." Then a single sentence: "Exposure targets specified in this document override requirements defined by other Articles of the Stability Scope."

That is a supremacy clause pointing in an unusual direction. The other Articles of the Stability Scope are the Risk Capital framework (A.3.2) and Asset Liability Management (A.3.3) — capital requirements, concentration limits, aggregate exposure ceilings and peg-reserve minimums. A yield-strategy document is asserting priority over the prudential rules that constrain it.

The practical target is identifiable. A.3.4.5.2.1 empowers the Core Facilitator to "trigger Executive Votes that instruct Arranged Structures to set up mechanisms that allow them to take direct exposure to Ethena sUSDe, or use legal rails to get direct exposure through custodians" — and Ethena is the single most tightly constrained exposure in the Scope, with a 1.3bn USDS aggregate ceiling allocated by name to Spark and Grove and zero for everyone else (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2.3).

So the override and the sUSDe provision read together: exposure taken through Arranged Structures and custodial legal rails at the Core Facilitator's initiative is not bound by the Ethena Exposure Limits, the Instance Financial CRR schedule, or the concentration caps that bind Prime Agents doing the same thing onchain.

Whether that is a considered carve-out or drafting overreach is not resolvable from the text, and the tension is worth flagging on both readings. Two mitigations exist in the same Section — every such mechanism requires an Executive Vote, so token holders authorize each instance, and the strategies run through Arranged Structures subject to the Arranger containment and reporting rules. But the general lesson holds regardless: a risk framework's strength is set by its weakest exemption clause, and this one exempts an entire class of exposure from the framework by reference rather than by argument.
description: A.3.4.5.1 states exposure targets in that document 'override requirements defined by other Articles of the Stability Scope', and the same Section routes direct sUSDe exposure through legal rails.
